name: Recorder
about: Record from any mic — phone, headset, Bluetooth, USB and lavaliers; trim, noise reduction, compression
dev.speaker: Phone speaker
lavHint: A lavalier or wireless system. Its noise cancellation, gain and modes are set on the receiver or in the maker’s app (Hollyland LarkSound, DJI Mimo) — their protocols are closed. To avoid double processing, keep noise reduction off here if it is on at the receiver.
btHint: A Bluetooth headset records over the voice channel: lower quality (16 kHz), like a phone call. For music, a wired, USB mic or a lavalier with a USB receiver is better.
rawHint: Clean sound without system noise suppression and auto gain — for music
devHint: Connected headphones, Bluetooth, USB mics and lavalier receivers appear in the list automatically. The input is chosen before recording, the output for listening.
devHintWeb: In the browser, device names appear after mic permission; output selection isn’t in every browser. Full input and output choice is in the Android app.
fx.lowcutHint: Removes rumble, wind and thumps below 80 Hz
fxHint: Processing doesn’t change the original: “Processed” to listen, “Save” to write it to the media library.
discardText: It hasn’t been saved to the media library and will be lost.
micDenied: No microphone access. It can be allowed in the phone settings.
micNone: The microphone is unavailable — another app may be using it.
m.clipAria: Clip: lights when the level hit the threshold. Tap to reset
m.hint: For music, keep peaks around −12…−6 dBFS: headroom before clipping, and normalization will raise the loudness. The CLIP light blinks when the level reached the threshold; “∞” keeps it lit until tapped.
help.1: Input and output — phone, headset, Bluetooth, USB.
help.2: Processing is heard before recording; after — trim, denoise, compare.
help.3: Red lamp — clipping: lower the input. The original stays intact.
help.tip: Denoise needs a second of silence at the start.
live.title: Sound before recording
live.off: The input is not being listened to — tap the wave above.
live.hint: Gain, EQ, low cut, compression and reverb are heard right away — in headphones, if the headphones icon is on. The original is written to the file; processing with these same settings is applied on save, as are noise reduction, gate and normalisation. Through the speaker without headphones, feedback may whistle.
